watercolours of various subjects, from the mundane, to the extraordinary
By Rula Jebreal
A collection of drawings, sketches, and collages by Palestinian artist Abdel-Bari Abbo, who is currently held in jail in Egypt, is currently showing at the Beirut Museum, titled "The artist in jail".
This is a unique exhibition, as the works have been collected and assembled by Abbo's friends in Egypt in jail. The exhibition includes around 50 of Abbo's sketches, etchings and watercolours of various subjects, from the mundane, to the extraordinary. The exhibition, open until August 19, is a unique artistic contribution by an individual, to illustrate what is happening in Egypt at the moment and what has been taking place in Egypt since September 2015, and is a symbol of the struggles against the prison regime in Egypt.

“I like the way things are made and how they work,” says Katherine, a Grade 12 student in Guelph who is planning to attend university to study mechanical engineering. “I like the way things function and work as a system together. I’ve never really taken a class in that, but I’m naturally interested in that and that’s why I’m doing engineering.”

This year at the Guelph Collegiate Institute, she’s on the engineering team that won the first annual University of Guelph Collegiate Institute Engineering Student Challenge in early June. The challenge challenged students from the college to come up with solutions to problems facing older Canadians, and Katherine’s team — named the Age Friendly Design Group — won by developing an app to make life easier for older Canadians and give them the opportunity to stay independent.

The app will be used for people who are living in retirement homes
